drivingQuestion: What does the mishna's clause about vowing a third party's valuation add over the earlier clause about one's own?
outcomeNote: The redundancy is answered from the latter clause, and the novelty of that clause is stated.

segments.he: הַיְינוּ הָךְ! סֵיפָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, דָּמָיו שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלָיו, וּמֵת הַנּוֹדֵר — יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁים.
segments.en: If so, «this» clause in the mishna is identical to «that» previous clause in the mishna, which states that if one said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and he dies, his heirs must give his valuation to the Temple treasury. Since it was explained that the earlier clause is also dealing with a case where he stood in judgment, for what purpose was this halakha repeated in the mishna? The Gemara answers: «It was necessary» to repeat this halakha in order to teach «the latter clause» of the mishna: With regard to one who says it is incumbent «upon him» to donate «the assessment of so-and-so, and the one who vowed dies,» his «heirs must give» his assessment to the Temple treasury.

segments.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֲמָדוּהוּ לָא אִישְׁתַּעְבּוּד נִכְסֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: כֵּיוָן דְּעָמַד בַּדִּין אִישְׁתַּעְבּוֹדֵי אִישְׁתַּעְבּוּד נִכְסֵי, וְאוּמְדָּנָא גַּלּוֹיֵי מִילְּתָא בְעָלְמָא הוּא.
segments.en: This is necessary «lest you say:» Although the one who took the vow stood in judgment before he died and the court obligated him, «since» the object of his vow «was not assessed» before he died, «the property of» the one who vowed «is not liened» to the debt, and consequently the heirs are not obligated to pay. Therefore, the mishna «teaches us» that «the property of» the one who took the vow «was liened, since he stood in judgment» while he was still alive, and «the assessment» of the object of the vow «is» considered to be «a mere disclosure of the matter,» which can be performed after the death of the one who vowed.
